subject.title: Feature Request: Gateway lifecycle hooks (onSubagentComplete, onToolCallThreshold, onTurnComplete)

question: Should OpenClaw expose subagent completion, turn completion, and tool-call threshold boundaries through HOOK.md workspace/internal hooks, typed plugin hooks only, or a split surface with different payload and authority levels?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the API choice affects trusted local code execution, session-state exposure, hook ordering, possible threshold config, and the boundary between operator automation and plugin middleware.

options.title: Split Observation From Control
options.body: Expose only minimal observation-oriented workspace events first, while keeping result mutation, threshold policy, and richer payloads in typed plugin hooks.

options.title: Typed Plugin Hooks Only
options.body: Avoid new HOOK.md lifecycle events and extend the plugin API for lifecycle or receipt use cases that need stronger contracts.

options.title: Full Workspace Surface
options.body: Add subagent, turn-complete, and threshold workspace events after maintainers define payload, ordering, redaction, and config semantics.

recommendation.title: Split Observation From Control
recommendation.body: Expose only minimal observation-oriented workspace events first, while keeping result mutation, threshold policy, and richer payloads in typed plugin hooks.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the internal hooks system and is the most direct routing candidate for a product/security boundary decision about workspace hook authority.
